2) The rigidity modulus of a material is defined as the ratio of

explanations.a: Stress to strain defines Young's modulus.
explanations.b: Correct! Rigidity modulus is the ratio of shear stress to shear strain. Read more
explanations.c: This defines bulk modulus, not rigidity modulus.
explanations.d: Tensile stress to tensile strain defines Young's modulus.

questions.question: 3) In the torsional pendulum experiment, increasing the radius of the suspension wire will

answers.d: Have no effect on the result

explanations.a: The radius affects the torsional constant, not directly the time period.
explanations.b: Rigidity modulus is a material property and not affected by geometry.
explanations.c: Correct! Torsional constant is proportional to the fourth power of the radius. See formula
explanations.d: Radius has a significant effect on torsional constant.

questions.question: 4) The expression for the rigidity modulus n derived from the torsional pendulum experiment involves which of the following quantities?

answers.a: Moment of inertia and angular velocity
answers.b: Mass of disc and angular displacement
answers.c: Length, radius of wire, and time period of oscillation

questions.question: 5) What is the formula used to calculate the rigidity modulus 'n' of the suspension wire in a torsion pendulum experiment when using two identical masses at different distances?

explanations.a: This is the formula for rigidity modulus when moment of inertia and period are directly used, not specific to identical masses at different distances.
explanations.b: This is the correct formula derived for the rigidity modulus using two identical masses at distances d1 and d2, as per equation (13) in the theory.
explanations.c: This is the formula for couple per unit twist (C), not the rigidity modulus.
explanations.d: This is an incorrect rearrangement of the torsion pendulum formula.
